name: Cable Hip Adduction
cues: Stand side-on to a low pulley with the strap on your near ankle
Step away until the cable holds that leg slightly out to the side
Sweep the strapped leg across in front of your standing leg
Stay upright and let the leg return slowly

qa.note: Family review 2026-10-01 rated minor. review: Two fixes. The balance counted the body only, so the pressure point sat 0.2 mm inside the inner edge of the foot; it now includes the cable and has a 41 mm margin. The finish moved from -4 to -2 deg adduction so the thighs stay inside the 15 mm tolerance, and the flexion ease moved so the floor guard never switches on. The foot still ends across, in front of the standing foot. For the owner: the stack top is clipped, and the grab arm is held straight out at shoulder height. | skeptic: Pelvis is level and the trunk upright, and the adductor is tinted on the right only. The cue 'Sweep the strapped leg across in front of your standing leg' is only partly shown. At the finish (ph 0) the working ball is at x 43 mm while the stance ball is at x 99 (foot about 96 mm wide), so the working foot stops just about at the stance foot's inner edge, 16 cm forward with hip flexion 30 and adduction -2. It never crosses the midline, and the adduction ends at about neutral. Also, the report's 'grab arm straight out at shoulder height' is wrong: by FK the grab elbow is 83-93 deg with the upper arm at 26-28 deg elevation (the forearm points at the lens). That is fine, just not what was reported. Stack top clipped. | skeptic: The adduction sweep reads in the hero (figure-515.png, adductor tint on the working thigh) and in the front sheet. The owner should judge three things. The stack top is clipped. The grab arm is held straight out at shoulder height, which looks stiff. At the finish (t=0.875/t=0) the working foot ends across, in front of the stance foot. In the front view the adductor tint is only a thin sliver (front/figure-515-front.png).
